Let \(x\) be the mass of NaHCO₃ and \(15.00-x\) be the mass of MgCO₃.

Molar masses:
- NaHCO₃ = 84.006 g/mol
- Na₂CO₃ = 105.988 g/mol
- MgCO₃ = 84.313 g/mol
- MgO = 40.304 g/mol

Residue from NaHCO₃:
\[
2\text{NaHCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3
\]
\[
\text{mass residue from NaHCO}_3 = x \times \frac{105.988}{2 \times 84.006}
\]

Residue from MgCO₃:
\[
\text{MgCO}_3 \rightarrow \text{MgO}
\]
\[
\text{mass residue from MgCO}_3 = (15.00-x) \times \frac{40.304}{84.313}
\]

Total residue:
\[
x \frac{105.988}{168.012} + (15.00-x)\frac{40.304}{84.313} = 8.80
\]

Solving gives:
\[
x = 10.664 \text{ g}
\]

Mass percentage of NaHCO₃:
\[
\frac{10.664}{15.00} \times 100 = 71.1\%
\]

ANSWER: 71.1
